SPHEREx / DR1 + QR3 · 0.75–5.0 μm · NASA / JPL / Caltech

02 / THROUGH THE GLASS

Down the telescope,
out into the deep sky.

From a telescope on a hill to one in orbit: SPHEREx surveys the sky in infrared light from 0.75 to 5.0 μm. Asterlight reads its released exposures straight from NASA/IPAC IRSA.

  • 0.75–5.0μm wavelength range
  • 6infrared detectors
  • DR1 + QR3public releases

    How the images are processed ↗

    A FIELD GUIDE TO LOOKING CLOSER

    Change is a clue.
    Context is the evidence.

    Asterlight makes the first look easier. A possible moving source still needs careful follow-up.

    Built for Planet X and SPHEREx, 2026 ↗
    1. 01

      Start with a fixed piece of sky.

      All frames are mapped to the same north-up coordinates. Black borders are missing coverage; purple pixels are masked quality flags.

    2. 02

      Compare like with like.

      SPHEREx samples different infrared wavelengths across a detector. Use similar wavelengths for comparison. Difference mode requires overlapping central bandpasses.

    3. 03

      Look for a consistent pattern.

      Motion should repeat across observations. Brightness alone can change with wavelength, background, resolution, and image artifacts. The two Epsilon Indi B components are not resolved here; WISE 0855 may be too faint in an individual exposure.

    4. 04

      Keep enough information to check.

      Export the observing log with coordinates, dates, URLs, quality flags, and your notes. Follow the original FITS links for scientific analysis.
